title: Reading Drill — Testing a lower stage for assemblies — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Testing a lower stage for assemblies — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The hall technician had been asked to investigate speakers becoming harder to see from the back in Hillswick. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on the distance at which a speaker's face is clear, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a six-week comparison, the team used seat-by-seat checks at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because differences in audience height might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward staggered rows. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
